page: Amazon Web Services c9g.48xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by the custom AWS Graviton9 Neoverse-V3 processor. Operating on the arm64 architecture at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz, this instance features 192 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core. The memory configuration consists of 384.0 GB of RAM, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. It utilizes the AWS Nitro hypervisor, lacks local storage, and does not include integrated GPUs.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 380393.63 and a PassMark CPU score of 106962.52. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 729.09 GB/sec for large-block read-only operations and 340.16 GB/sec for large-block write operations. The server demonstrates strong capabilities in data processing, achieving 1910.26 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and 511.16 million operations per second in Redis SET operations. However, single-core performance is moderate, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2006.19.

Equipped with a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps, the c9g.48xlarge is designed for high-throughput network tasks. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high density of dedicated ARMv9 physical cores provides substantial compute capacity per resource unit without hyperthreading overhead. This profile is highly suited for multi-threaded workloads, high-concurrency web serving, database operations, and prompt processing for medium-sized language models, though it is less optimal for tasks requiring local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration.
